description: Proposes rezoning 831 5th Avenue North for a six-unit multi-dwelling.
Includes two affordable housing units at $1090 monthly.
Residents raised concerns about parking and neighborhood character.

chips.text: Councillor McDonald advocated for infrastructure investment in established neighborhoods.
Public expressed concerns about the number of multi-unit dwellings and exceeding HAF limits.

description: Rezones 831 5th Avenue North to RM3 district.
Allows up to six dwelling units on the site.
Includes eight on-street parking spaces.
Amends zoning for 105 Avenue F South.
Removes specific grocery and dry goods reporting requirements.
Allows up to six smaller retail units in the building.

chips.text: Councillor clarified food sales would still be permitted, not prohibited.
TCRT Investments applied for the zoning agreement amendment.
No public comments or presentations were received on the application.

description: Amends downtown MX-2 zoning, setting 27-meter height maximum.
Allows density bonuses, reduces retail size, permits daycares.
Prohibits drive-throughs, low-density housing; effective January 1, 2026.

chips.text: One advanced housing project accommodated by delayed effective date.
Municipal Planning Commission recommended consideration without concerns.

description: Updates downtown zoning density bonus provisions.
Allows taller buildings for public benefits in B6, MX2 districts.
Adds affordable housing, bike parking as new public benefits.

chips.text: Mayor Block clarified new affordable housing and bike parking provisions.
Modernizes unused 2015 density bonus system to encourage downtown development.
Sustainable building certification is a new density bonus provision.

description: Designates standalone surface parking as discretionary in B6, MX2, M4 zones.
Prohibits new standalone parking lots on 2nd Avenue, 21st Street.
Introduces temporary surface parking lot option.
Requires landscaping for all surface parking lots.

chips.text: Owners of approximately 15 illegal downtown parking lots face enforcement.
Administration historically took an "accommodating approach" to illegal surface parking lots.
Administration received no significant public opposition or concern.
Administration will proactively investigate and enforce against 15 illegal downtown parking lots.

description: Proposes housekeeping amendments to Zoning Bylaw No. 9990.
Clarifies rules for digital and EMC billboards.
Planning Commission supports proposed bylaw amendments.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer questioned if NSPA concerns were addressed in this phase.
Administration confirmed NSPA's sign regulation concerns will be addressed in phase two.

description: Proposes changing land use to rural commercial industrial.
Located southeast of Saskatoon, east of Highway 16.
Could create 830 jobs at full build-out.
